user.title: Add a KNX scene tracker (1/2)
user.description: Track a KNX scene: activating it sends a DPT 18.001 recall telegram (KNX applies its own stored values), and a matching learn (store) telegram on this group address for this scene number snapshots the selected entities' current state into the scene.

data_description.scene_name: A friendly name for this tracker. Purely cosmetic - has no effect on entity ids or KNX communication, so it's safe to change any time.
data_description.group_address: The KNX group address your scene control object (DPT 18.001) is wired to in ETS. Both the learn (store) and recall (activate) telegrams for this scene use this same address.
data_description.ga_type: DPT 18.001 (default) supports both recall and learn - the KNX Learn Scene button and KNX-side learning are available. DPT 17.001 is a plain 1-byte scene number with no control bit, so it's recall-only - no way to signal 'store' on the wire. Choosing DPT 17.001 removes the Learn button entirely, since there's no valid telegram it could send. Recall, state feedback, and the Snapshot Entities button work identically either way.
data_description.scene_number: The KNX scene number this tracker corresponds to on that group address, 1-64. Must be unique per group address - one GA can have up to 64 different tracked scenes, each with its own number.
data_description.entities: The KNX-provided entities (lights, switches, etc.) that make up this scene. Their combined state is what gets captured on snapshot, and what the state switch (next step) compares against to decide if the scene is active.
data_description.snapshot_now: On: capture the entities' current state into the scene immediately. Off: create the scene with no stored values yet - it will only get values from the first learn telegram, button press, or manual edit.

state_entity.title: Add a KNX scene tracker (2/2) - state switch
state_entity.description: This next step configures the state switch - a separate entity from the scene itself, created automatically for every tracker, that answers one question: is this scene active right now? It compares the live state of every entity from the previous step against what was captured on the last snapshot, so it reflects reality even if the scene was never actually activated - for example if someone just happened to set the lights to matching values by hand. Comparison is exact by default, though a small tolerance can be allowed for numeric attributes like brightness (see below) to absorb KNX<->HA rounding drift. It's a real switch (not just a sensor) so it's controllable too: switching it on activates the scene (the same as pressing Activate on the Scene entity itself), and switching it off runs whichever Off action you choose below. Being controllable is also what makes it usable as a HomeKit accessory later, if you expose it through Home Assistant's HomeKit Bridge.

data.off_scene_entity: Scene to activate when off (if Off action is 'Activate another scene')

data_description.state_group_address: Optional. If set, this scene's active/inactive status is pushed to this KNX group address and answers GroupValueRead requests from other KNX devices. Leave blank and the state switch still works normally within Home Assistant (including HomeKit exposure) - it just won't have a status visible on the KNX bus. Must be unique across all your trackers.
data_description.off_action: What happens when the state switch is turned off (e.g. from HomeKit). 'No action' leaves it purely reflecting live state - toggling off doesn't do anything by itself. 'Activate another scene' calls scene.turn_on on the scene picked below - typically a matching 'off' tracker, keeping both directions KNX-driven. 'Turn all entities off' turns off everything listed on the previous step directly.
data_description.off_scene_entity: Only used when Off action is 'Activate another scene'. Any scene entity, not just ones tracked by this integration.
data_description.numeric_tolerance: Default 1. 0 means exact match. KNX's DPT 5.001 percentage scaling and Home Assistant's 0-255 brightness scale don't convert losslessly - 50% can come back as 127 or 126 depending on rounding direction - so a strict comparator can flicker 'inactive' on scenes that are, for all practical purposes, exactly right. Raise this further to absorb more drift. Only applies to numeric attribute values (brightness, current_position, temperature, etc.) - the on/off state itself is always compared exactly.
data_description.debounce_seconds: Default 1.5s. How long to wait after a tracked entity's state changes before recomputing whether the scene is active. Coalesces a burst of near-simultaneous changes (several lights settling after a scene recall) into one recompute instead of many. Different entity types settle at different speeds - a plain switch is near-instant, a slow cover keeps reporting position updates throughout its travel - so tune this per tracker if needed.
